title: Implementation discipline
summary: Implementation MUST remain within the approved plan, establish deterministic pre-edit repository-check baselines, run only blast-radius tests while iterating, and directly remediate every cause of a retry.
instructions: Each material change MUST map to an acceptance criterion or an explicitly documented enabling change.
Agents MUST NOT redesign adjacent systems unless the approved plan requires it.

Before the first coder invocation, the harness MUST run and persist a baseline for each interior gate profile. An interior gate profile is a profile other than full that a source-allowed stage gate references under the run's verification level. Under every built-in level the interior gate profiles are static and fast. The full profile MUST NOT run as a baseline. The baseline makes a pre-existing failure distinguishable from a regression.

The coder MUST inspect the pre-implementation static and fast baselines before editing. Existing failures MUST be repaired when bounded and low-risk; an unchanged pre-existing failure MUST NOT block the workflow when remediation would be broad, structural, or unrelated to the approved change. Any new or worsened diagnostic MUST remain a hard failure.

On implementation attempt 2 or later, the coder MUST perform work that directly addresses every issue causing the retry and MUST populate implementation.remediation with cause, action, and evidence. A paperwork-only retry is prohibited.

After each group of changes, the coder MUST run the impacted iteration profile plus every test it added. In self-development that profile is `pan tests impacted`, which selects modules by static import-graph analysis. In a target installation the coder MUST use the target's declared impacted profile. Only when no impacted profile exists, the coder MUST select the tests in the immediate blast radius by judgment. Every test command MUST derive from runtime/repository-checks.json or the target's documented test entry points. The coder MUST NOT guess a test command. The coder MAY run the static profile freely.

The impacted mapping does not reach every changed path. When a changed path yields no impacted test, the coder MUST choose a judgment cohort of tests that cover that path, and MUST NOT treat the empty selection as an absent blast radius. It MUST record each unreached path and its chosen cohort. Cohort selection is judgment-only and carries no deterministic check.
Each added test MUST appear in tests_added with the contract it proves.

When the coder believes the change is complete, it MUST run the fast profile once as validation. After a failure, the coder MUST fix the cause and MUST re-run only the impacted selection and the failing tests. The coder MAY run the fast profile before that validation run when the impacted selection exceeds the advisory threshold or when a failure reproduces only under the fast lane. The advisory threshold is the one the impacted tool reports. The coder MUST NOT substitute its own estimate of the blast radius for that report. The coder MUST NOT repeat the fast run after validation unless the blast radius is exceptionally large. That threshold is high, because the verify and remediate stages catch what slips.
On a retry attempt that changed only output claims or evidence, the coder MUST NOT run any test profile. The retry MUST cite the evidence of the prior run.

The harness MUST rerun declared deterministic gates independently on any submission that can still succeed. The next instruction names the one exception: an accepted recorded pass. A non-success outcome is a declared failure or blocked result, a failed hard self-criterion, or a failed read attestation. When the submitted output already decides a non-success outcome, the harness MUST NOT execute shell gate commands. The harness MUST record each affected gate as skipped with the deciding reason.

The harness MAY accept a recorded clean pass of the identical gate command instead of re-executing it. Acceptance needs an unchanged Git workspace fingerprint and an unchanged repository-check configuration. Acceptance needs a record under 24 hours old and a resolved run baseline. An accepted pass MUST be marked cached. An accepted pass MUST carry the original captured output as its evidence. An accepted pass MUST NOT be a failure, timeout, skip, override, or baseline-relative credit. PAN_GATE_CACHE=0 disables acceptance.

Before submission, the implementation record, changed-file claims, retry-remediation evidence, acceptance evidence, and referenced summary artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.

The fast/default profile MUST contain only deterministic offline tests. Tests that make real external network or catalog calls MUST be marked and confined to a secondary, integration, or full-only profile.

Elapsed clock time alone MUST NOT fail a repository check that exits successfully. A slow successful check MUST be recorded as an operator FYI; a timeout, hang, nonzero exit, or new diagnostic remains actionable.
